label: last copy step, previous output in {2,l,i,g} and final output in {2,n,o,q,u}, short sequences
predicate: (phase == 2) & (to_go == 0) & isin(in_tok, [tok("2"), tok("l"), tok("i"), tok("g")]) & isin(out_tok, [tok("2"), tok("n"), tok("o"), tok("q"), tok("u")]) & (L <= 4)
explanation: A sparse copy-phase feature: 98.5% of its activation mass is in the copy phase, it never fires at the delimiter, and it almost never fires in the original phase. 86% of the mass is on the final copy step (to_go == 0), where the input is the fed-back token orig(L-2) and the output is orig(L-1). Most of the rest is one step earlier. The input token is almost always 2, l, i or g (97% of mass). The output token tends to be 2, n, o, q or u, and activity is much higher for short sequences (L = 3-4 hold 58% of the mass; rate drops sharply for L >= 7). The strongest activations are length-3/4 sequences such as o l o <DEL> o [l] and l i o <DEL> l [i]. These cues are necessary but nowhere near sufficient: input-token plus final-step alone has about 2% precision, and the feature also depends on earlier tokens such as the first token (o, l, 2, n favored). That looks like a conjunctive hidden-state code rather than one clean variable. Best simple predicate: dev F1 about 0.30. It does not fire on other input letters (a-f, etc.) or on the delimiter.
